analysis.title: Prime Services Weekly Report, October 9, 2026 (Friday 10/2 – Thursday 10/8)
key_insights: GS Equity Fundamental L/S performance estimate fell -0.70% from 10/2 to 10/8 vs MSCI World TR +0.78%. The loss came almost entirely from alpha, with both long and short side losses, while beta finished about flat.
GS Equity Systematic L/S performance estimate rose +0.82% over the same week, with alpha of +0.55% from short side gains and beta of +0.27%.

Overall book gross leverage rose 0.7 pts to 308.7% (60th percentile 1-year). Net leverage fell 1.5 pts to 75.9% (10th percentile 1-year). Overall book L/S ratio fell 1.2% to 1.652 (14th percentile 1-year).
Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 3.3 pts to 209.5% (43rd percentile 1-year). Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 0.2 pts to 52.9% (6th percentile 1-year).
Global equities were net sold (-0.3 SDs 1-year). Gross trading activity kept rising, with short sales outpacing long buys 1.3 to 1.

All major regions except Europe were net sold, led in dollar terms by North America and EM Asia. Europe saw long buys of +1.80 SDs and Japan saw short sales of -2.35 SDs, the largest regional changes in trading flows.
Macro products were net sold, driven by short sales. Single stocks saw little net activity because short sales were offset by a roughly equal amount of long buys.
TMT sectors (Info Tech + Comm Svcs) and Materials were the most net sold global sectors in dollar terms. Industrials, Consumer Discretionary and Health Care were the most net bought.

US Info Tech was by far the most net sold US sector (-1.0 SDs 1-year), driven by long and short sales, after being the most net bought US sector in 4 of the past 5 weeks. The desk reads this as profit taking and more hedging, most notably on Thursday Oct 8.
Within US Info Tech, Tech Hardware, Storage & Peripherals and Semis & Semi Equip were the most net sold subsectors, while Software was the most net bought.

US Info Tech L/S ratio is 1.8 (-3.8% w/w), in the 31st percentile vs. the past year and the 17th vs. the past five years. Gross/Net allocation is 21.5%/20.4% of US exposure, in the 87th/83rd percentiles over one year and the 97th/80th over five years.

HFs net sold US Consumer Staples for a 3rd straight week (7 of the last 8), driven entirely by short sales. Household Products and Staples Distribution & Retail selling outpaced modest buying in Food, Beverage & Tobacco.

US Consumer Staples L/S ratio is 0.9 (-1.5% w/w), in the 14th percentile vs. the past year and the 3rd vs. the past five years. Gross/Net allocation is 4.1%/-0.4%, in the 5th/17th percentiles over one year.
The largest sector flow changes were in Real Estate, with long buys of +2.10 SDs and short sales of -1.98 SDs.

sector_views.rationale: HFs net sold US Info Tech at the fastest pace in 7 weeks (-1.0 SDs), reflecting profit taking and hedging, yet gross/net allocation remains high at 21.5%/20.4% of US exposure.
HFs net sold US Consumer Staples for a 3rd straight week, driven by short sales. Net allocation is -0.4% of US exposure and L/S ratio is 0.9.

risk_factors: Net leverage at the 10th percentile 1-year (6th for Fundamental L/S) means hedge funds are running low net exposure.
Elevated Info Tech positioning (87th percentile gross allocation over 1 year, 97th over 5 years) alongside the largest net selling in 7 weeks.
